title: How does Airframe use aircraft settings?
summary: Optionally add propeller size, blade count, and motor layout to give Overview, the craft presentation, and aircraft-aware guides useful physical context.
questions: Which aircraft details can I add?
Where does Airframe use these details?
When should I correct an automatic result?

blocks.text: Aircraft Settings add optional physical context to the logs in an Airframe document. Propeller size makes frequency regions more relevant to the craft, blade count enables expected blade-pass orders, and motor layout keeps the craft presentation oriented correctly.

steps: Save the raw log as an Airframe document if it is not already part of one.
Open Overview and find the Aircraft card.
Choose Customize and select the Propeller Size used for the recording.
Review Propeller Blades and Motor Layout. A spinner means Airframe is still examining the log for a possible value.
Use the info button to review an automatic result, correct anything that does not match the aircraft, and choose Save if you want to keep those values with the document.

blocks.caption: Where each aircraft setting helps
rows: Frequency regions suited to the size and type of craft.
Expected blade-pass orders in Frequency vs RPM.
Choose 2, 3, 4, or Other / Unknown. Airframe may find 2 or 3 from the log.
The matching craft orientation and layout-aware results such as the center-of-gravity estimate.
Choose the layout that matches the aircraft or review Airframe's result.

blocks.title: Automatic blade detection is deliberately conservative
blocks.text: Airframe can identify two- or three-blade props when the log contains a clear relationship between frequency and motor RPM. A detected count is immediately available to the Spectrum guides. Four blades and recordings without clear enough evidence remain choices for you to make.

blocks.title: Other / Unknown is a useful answer
blocks.text: Choose Other / Unknown when none of the listed options describes the aircraft or when you cannot verify the value. Airframe keeps the missing context visible instead of building a guide from a guess.

blocks.title: Aircraft context makes views more specific

blocks.text: Overview shows the effective aircraft details beside the recorded setup evidence. Graph uses Motor Layout for the craft presentation. Spectrum uses Propeller Size for craft-specific frequency regions and a numeric Blade Count for blade-pass guides. These details add context; they do not change the recorded data, FFT, Filter Delay, System Response, Tune Score, or automatic ratings.
The Spectrum guide explains how Frequency, Frequency vs Throttle, and Frequency vs RPM answer different questions, and how to compare a moving ridge with the blade-pass lines.
